# Review: Aeration Control Narrative (before release to contractor)

**Verdict: do not release.** The narrative has three technical conflicts (items F-01, F-02, F-03) and several undefined behaviors. A contractor could not build or test it as written. It also lacks the structure a FAT needs: no module boundaries, no state table, no requirement IDs, no sequences, and no abnormal handling.

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | Para 2 vs 5 | Units conflict. 7.5 psig is about 208 inH2O. The staging thresholds (160 and 165 inH2O) are about 5.8 and 6.0 psig. | Use one unit (psig) for all pressures. See SP-002, SP-010 and SP-011. |
| F-02 | Para 2 and 5 | The staging logic cannot work. With the header held near its setpoint, the stage-off threshold is always exceeded, so a running blower stages off at once. The stage-on threshold is reached only after the header has already collapsed. Pressure is also the controlled variable, so it is a poor staging trigger. | Stage on from sustained high blower loading or a sustained pressure shortfall. Stage off from sustained low loading with enough remaining capacity. See SP-010 to SP-015. |
| F-03 | Para 2 | "Fixed setpoint" contradicts the most-open-valve (MOV) reset in the next sentence. | State that the setpoint is initial and the maximum, with MOV trim below it. Define the limits and rate in SP-002 to SP-005. |
| F-04 | Para 2 | The MOV logic is incomplete. It lacks a deadband, an exclusion rule for valves that are in manual, failed or out of service, and a rule for when the blowers are at their limit. | Add the exclusions and the limit behavior (FR-AER-012 to 014). |
| F-05 | Para 2 | The narrative does not say what the header pressure controller manipulates (IGV, speed or blow-off). Surge and minimum-flow protection are missing. | Name the final element and tags per blower. Add surge and minimum-flow behavior. These come from the blower vendor (open item OI-03). |
| F-06 | Para 3 | Closing the valve on DO signal loss is unsafe for the process. It starves the biology, stops mixing and can dead-head the blowers. | Hold the last position briefly, then go to a fixed fallback position. Never close fully. Exclude the basin from MOV. See SP-006 to SP-008. |
| F-07 | Para 1 | No loop definition: control action, modes, bad-PV criteria, output limits, or the FCV fail position. | Add a regulatory table per loop (FR-AER-001 to 004). |
| F-08 | Para 4 | The permissive is incomplete. ZSC-931 is a single tag for three blowers. The discharge valve has no tag. Lube, starter-ready, trip-reset, local/remote and restart-timer conditions are missing. | Write the per-blower permissive rows in section C below. |
| F-09 | Whole document | No start or stop sequence, no timeouts, no failure responses. | Use the step table in section D. |
| F-10 | Para 6 | Restarting all blowers at once on power return causes inrush and voltage sag. No stagger, outage limit or trip exclusion. | See FR-AER-030 to 033 and SP-020 to SP-022. |
| F-11 | Para 7 | The vibration trip has no tags, value, delay, latch, reset or start bypass. It also does not say whether it is a SIS function or vendor machinery protection. | See interlock row IL-05 and open item OI-02. |
| F-12 | Whole document | No states or modes (ISA-106), no automation level, no purpose or boundaries, no operator interface, no alarms, no comms-loss or PIT-920 failure handling, no requirement IDs, no test methods, no open items. | Add all of these using the template. Section E gives the abnormal handling. |
| F-13 | Para 1 to 7 | Numbers sit in prose (2.0 mg/L, 7.5 psig, 85%, 160/165, 2 min). | Move them to the setpoint list. |
| F-14 | Whole document | Wording is not STE-compliant ("maintain", "adjusts", "on loss of"). Equipment is not tagged (B-1/2/3, discharge valve). | Run the STE pass after the content is settled. Tag every item. |

## A. Setpoint list (none was supplied; all values are provisional unless noted)

| ID | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| SP-001 | 2.0 | mg/L | From narrative. Confirm with the process designer. |
| SP-002 | 7.5 | psig | From narrative. Use as the maximum header setpoint. Confirm. |
| SP-003 | 5.5 | psig | Minimum header setpoint. Confirm. |
| SP-004 | 85 | % | MOV target, from narrative. |
| SP-005 | 5 | % | MOV deadband. Confirm. |
| SP-006 | 10 | min | Hold time after DO signal loss. Confirm. |
| SP-007 | 30 | % | Fallback valve position after hold time. Confirm. |
| SP-008 | 10 | % | Minimum valve position for mixing. Confirm. |
| SP-009 | 0.1 | psi/min | Maximum header setpoint change rate. Confirm. |
| SP-010 | 95 | % | Stage-on blower loading. Confirm. |
| SP-011 | 5 | min | Stage-on delay. Replaces the 2 min value in the narrative. Confirm. |
| SP-012 | 70 | % | Stage-off loading, calculated for the remaining blowers. Confirm. |
| SP-013 | 15 | min | Stage-off delay. Confirm. |
| SP-014 | 15 | min | Minimum run time. Confirm. |
| SP-015 | 10 | min | Minimum off time. Confirm. |
| SP-016 | 4 | starts/h | Maximum starts per blower. Confirm with the motor vendor. |
| SP-017 | 30 | s | IGV closed timeout. Confirm. |
| SP-018 | 60 | s | Discharge valve open timeout. Confirm. |
| SP-019 | 15 | s | Run feedback timeout. Confirm. |
| SP-020 | 60 | s | Restart stagger interval. Confirm. |
| SP-021 | 10 | min | Maximum outage for auto restart. Confirm. |
| SP-022 | 5 | s | Power-restore confirm time before the restart timer starts. Confirm. |
| SP-023 | 3 | s | Vibration trip delay. Confirm. |
| SP-024 | TBD | vendor units | Vibration alarm and trip values. Needs the blower vendor (OI-02). |

## B. Requirements to add (examples, each needs a test method)

- FR-AER-001: Each DO controller (AIT-901 to 904) acts reverse on FCV-911 to 914 and holds SP-001. *Test: step the setpoint, confirm valve direction.*
- FR-AER-004: Each FCV output is limited to SP-008 minimum in auto.
- FR-AER-010: The MOV logic lowers the PIT-920 setpoint when the most open valve is above SP-004 plus SP-005. It raises the setpoint when the valve is below SP-004 minus SP-005. The setpoint stays between SP-003 and SP-002 at a rate no faster than SP-009.
- FR-AER-012: The MOV logic ignores valves in manual, with a bad DO signal, or out of service.
- FR-AER-014: When all running blowers are at maximum output, the MOV logic stops lowering the setpoint and raises an alarm.
- FR-AER-020: Stage on a blower when loading exceeds SP-010 for SP-011. Stage off when the remaining blowers would load below SP-012 for SP-013. Respect SP-014 to SP-016.
- FR-AER-021: Rotate the lead blower by run hours.
- FR-AER-030 to 033: After power restore, wait SP-022, then restart previously running blowers one at a time at SP-020 intervals. Do this only if the outage was within SP-021, there is no active trip, and permissives are met. Do not restart a blower that tripped before the outage.

## C. Interlocks and permissives (no cause-and-effect chart was given)

Tag names for items marked * are proposed. Confirm them against the instrument index.

| ID | Cause | Effect | Latched or auto-reset | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IL-01 | B-x start permissives not met: ZSC-93x* IGV closed, ZSV-94x* discharge valve open, lube OK, starter ready, no trip, remote mode, min off time elapsed, start count under SP-016 | Block start | Auto-reset | Clears when the condition clears |
| IL-02 | Start step timeout (SP-017 to SP-019) | Abort start, alarm | Latched | Operator reset |
| IL-03 | Run feedback lost | Stop B-x, start next blower, alarm | Latched | Operator reset |
| IL-04 | PIT-920 bad | Hold blower output, alarm (see E) | Auto-reset | Signal good for 30 s |
| IL-05 | Vibration above SP-024 trip value for SP-023, bypassed during start | Trip B-x, IGV to closed, alarm | Latched | Local operator reset after cause cleared |

## D. Start sequence (B-x), proposed

| Step | Action | Transition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check permissives | All met | 5 s | Abort, alarm |
| 2 | Close IGV | ZSC-93x closed | SP-017 | Abort, alarm |
| 3 | Open discharge valve | Open limit made | SP-018 | Abort, alarm |
| 4 | Start motor | Run feedback true | SP-019 | Stop, latch IL-02 |
| 5 | Release IGV to pressure control | Output above minimum | 60 s | Hold, alarm |

The stop sequence needs the same table (unload, stop, close discharge valve). The state table (Stopped, Starting, Running, Stopping, Tripped) with exits and automation level is also missing.

## E. Abnormal handling to add

- **AIT-90x bad:** hold, then fall back per SP-006 to SP-008. Exclude from MOV. Alarm.
- **PIT-920 bad:** freeze the setpoint at its last value and hold blower output. Use a redundant transmitter if installed (OI-04). Alarm.
- **Blower comms loss:** treat the blower as unavailable. Do not stage it. Keep a running blower running under its local controls.
- **FCV air or power loss:** set the fail position (OI-05).
- **Power loss:** see FR-AER-030 to 033.

## F. Alarms needed (no database given)

Respond to each as follows. Rationalize priorities under ISA-18.2.

| Alarm | Response |
|---|---|
| AIT-90x bad signal | Check the probe. The basin is on fallback. |
| Header pressure low/high | Check the blowers and valves. |
| Blower start failure | Check the permissive that failed. |
| Blower vibration high / trip | Inspect before reset. |
| All blowers at maximum | Reduce demand or start a standby. |
| Blower auto restart held | Start manually. |

## G. Open items

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Confirm all provisional setpoints (SP-001 to SP-023) and operations sign-off on states and prompts | Process lead and operations | Before contractor release |
| OI-02 | Vibration alarm and trip values. Decide if the trip is a SIS function (then reference the SRS) or vendor machinery protection | Blower vendor and controls lead | Date to be set |
| OI-03 | Final element, surge, and minimum-flow behavior | Blower vendor | Date to be set |
| OI-04 | Redundant PIT-920 decision | Controls lead | Date to be set |
| OI-05 | FCV-911 to 914 fail positions | Process lead | Date to be set |
| OI-06 | Tag the blower discharge valves, IGVs and per-blower position switches in the instrument index | Consultant | Date to be set |

I left the due dates open because none were given. Assign them at the review meeting. The STE edit pass comes after the consultant has resolved F-01 to F-12.
